### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a8a4ac29e20278ee7741734aba314789409b14ab` — the merge of head `78bc99821f33eb9e2fafb83b91dfacffea5f6074` into base `d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a8a4ac29e20278ee7741734aba314789409b14ab && git checkout a8a4ac29e20278ee7741734aba314789409b14ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32 78bc99821f33eb9e2fafb83b91dfacffea5f6074 && git checkout -B drift-repro d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32 && git merge --no-ff 78bc99821f33eb9e2fafb83b91dfacffea5f6074

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d9c799c104a7cdcc429e4c6f04313043bd8a5b32` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81c369ca52a0fe89b5fd2edb4adeffd89f07a842`
Local-runs: probe — the one claim ④ turns on (no pattern QuickJS runs is refused) cannot be read off the diff or the check-runs, and the workspace has no install; quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0 was installed into the scratch directory alone and one script compiled the action wrapper text over a pattern list on Node 22.23.5 `node:vm` and on the release-sync `evalCode` (run twice: 136 hand-picked patterns, then every identifier in the wasm as a property name). Nothing in the repo was built, tested or re-run.
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-regexp-literal-token-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.body-regexp-pattern-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.hook-job-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts, packages/lint/src/checked-parse.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandboxed-action-crash-is-a-fault.test.ts

Read for it, not reviewed: `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts` (`mapDataError`), `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/observe.ts`, `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` on `main`, cards #35694, #35715, #35720, #36727.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, the three compile rules (`action-body-does-not-compile`, `hook-body-does-not-compile`, `job-body-does-not-compile`): a V8 pattern failure whose reason is not `Duplicate capture group name` or `Invalid group` moves from `warning` to `error` at `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` and the metadata publish door (422 for `action`, `object`, `hook` writes). Right as a narrowing: all three read the one `judgeBodyCompile`, and the shape ternary is the whole change. The card's six classes and both controls are pinned.
- Public surface, `@objectstack/lint`: `BodyCompileShape` gains `regexp-dialect-gap`; `regexp-pattern` changes severity. A consumer switching on the shape sees a new member: right, declared in the changeset.
- Public surface, `@objectstack/runtime`: the operator line of a hook or job compile failure moves from `KIND 'NAME' threw: SyntaxError…` to `KIND 'NAME' does not compile: SyntaxError…`. `innerMessage`, status and code are what the generic branch produced (same `userFacingMessage(formatErr(err))`, no status, no runner-own-fault mark), so `mapDataError` (which the REST and the MCP data doors both read) answers the same sanitised `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`. Right. The action branch builds the same two strings as before.
- Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`: one new ADR-0087 D3 entry, three sibling entries reworded, one TSDoc paragraph on `ScriptBodySchema`. No schema key, no accepted value moves. Right.
- Gates: every check-run on this head concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed (Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 10/10, Dogfood Regression Gate among them).

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are the right pair: a value an author could save (a body carrying such a pattern) is now refused, and nothing is widened. The `!` and the BREAKING banner follow from the arm. `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves; the changeset gives `minor` to `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec`, the same three the sibling changeset 34987 moved. The runtime's own change is a log sentence and would stand at `patch` alone; `minor` is not below the floor, so it is accepted. The changeset carries the FROM → TO list, the one-line fix and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered body-regexp-pattern-refused`).

`Skills-docs: follow-up #36727` is honest: #36727 is open, `Blocked-by: #36721`, names the one sentence on `main` (`data-hooks.md`, "A regex pattern the checking engine refuses is a warning: the runtime may accept it") and the rewrite it needs. The changeset's `follow-up owed` form names the same file. No other published skill teaches the split.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (claim said `Clause-②: no`, PR and changeset say `no (narrowing)`): answered, `no (narrowing)` is correct for a warning that became a refusal.
- Dev deviation 2 (six text-only files outside the claimed surface): answered, accepted. Each sentence was made false by this diff or is named by row #35720 N5; none changes behaviour.
- Dev deviations 3 and 4 (one push before the overlap re-check; footer form): process notes, no contract effect.
- `open_questions`: empty.
- Out-of-scope note, `mapDataError` drops `INTERNAL_ERROR` for a code-less declared 5xx: pre-existing, not reached by this diff (the hook and job branch declares no status); carrier none, left as noted.
- Out-of-scope note, stale `actionBodyCompileFailure` comment in `packages/core`: outside the diff, comment only.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff has no query.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: the spec declares that an L2 body runs inside the runtime's wrapper, and a pattern QuickJS refuses never ran, so refusing it makes the spec's own refusal real and takes nothing away. That holds for every row of the dev's table and for the further V8 reasons probed here (the `v`-flag class errors, `Lone quantifier brackets`, `Invalid named reference`, `Invalid decimal escape`, `Invalid property name in character class`: QuickJS refused each). It does not hold for one reason, below.

(b) Oracle agreement. The lint compiles `actionBodyFunctionExpression(source)` or `hookBodyFunctionExpression(source)` as a sloppy script with `node:vm`; the runner embeds the same expression, from the same two functions, in a sloppy global `evalCode` on `newQuickJSWASMModule()` (release-sync, 0.32.0 in the lockfile). Same text, same goal symbol, and QuickJS compiles a literal's pattern at parse, as V8's early error does. Agreed. `isCompileFailure` reads `name === 'SyntaxError'` on the `evalCode` error, which an async arrow's own throw cannot reach; the control pin (`JSON.parse` at run) covers it.

(d) Residual direction. The dev's stated residual (first V8 reason allow-listed, QuickJS also refuses) reproduces and errs toward a missed refusal. It is not the only gap, and the other one errs the wrong way:

S1 (should-fix) — `Invalid property name` is a third reason on which V8 refuses and QuickJS runs, and the rule sends it to `error`, so a body that runs is refused. Measured on Node 22.23.5 (ICU 78.3, Unicode 17) against quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0 release-sync, same wrapper text: under `u`, the property escapes `\p{IDS_Unary_Operator}` (alias `IDSU`), `\p{Modifier_Combining_Mark}` (alias `MCM`) and `\p{sc=Katakana_Or_Hiragana}` (alias `Hrkt`, also with `scx=`) answer V8 `Invalid property name` while QuickJS compiles them: 8 spellings out of 2896 candidate names tried in four forms. The same channel is wider on a host the packages still support (`engines` is Node 22.0.0 or later): V8 resolves property names through the host's ICU, an early Node 22 ships a Unicode 15.1 ICU, and QuickJS 0.32.0 accepted `Script=Garay`, `Script=Sidetic`, `Script=Tolong_Siki` and `scx=Beria_Erfe` (Unicode 16 and 17 scripts); that half is inferred from the ICU versions, not run. So these sentences are false as written: the surface of `18.body-regexp-pattern-refused.ts` ("a regular-expression literal whose pattern both engines refuse") and its reason ("every other reason probed (… Invalid property name …) QuickJS refuses too" reads as a fact about the reason, and the code acts on the reason); the module note of `validate-action-body-compiles.ts` ("a refusal missed, never a body that runs refused", "Every other pattern REASON is an `error`, because QuickJS refuses the pattern too"); the `regexp-pattern` hint and test titles ("the runtime's engine refuses it too"); `rule-explanations.ts` ("an unknown Unicode property … refused by both"). Realistic exposure is small (three rare property values on the pinned host), the PR's maintainer summary already names a runnable pattern refused as the worst case, and the card's done-when requires `/\p{Nope}/u` at `error`, so the reason cannot simply join the allow-list. Smallest fix that makes the contract true: keep the reason at `error`, and say in the entry, the module note and `os explain` that a Unicode property or script name is judged by the host's Unicode tables, naming the measured exceptions and the way out (build the expression with `new RegExp` at run time, which the dialect-gap hint already offers and the `regexp-pattern` hint does not). A measured exception list for those names at `warning` is the stronger fix and is the dev's choice.

(c) The other `hits` files hold. `hook-body.zod.ts`: the TSDoc now matches `action-body-wrapper.ts` (an async arrow taking `ctx` for hooks and jobs, and `input, ctx` for actions), where the old `new AsyncFunction` wording did not. `18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts` and `18.action-body-regexp-literal-token-refused.ts`: the reworded `replacement` matches the ternary (two reasons warn, the rest refused) and N4's line-terminator cause matches the unterminated hint. `18.hook-job-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts`: the narrowed job-door sentence and the run-time sentence match `authoring-rules.ts` and `bodyCompileFailure`. All three inherit S1 only through their pointer to the new entry.

Implementing files. `judgeBodyCompile`: the reason is the text after the last colon-space, which is safe because a pattern that itself contains such text sits before V8's reason; token errors (`missing /`, `flags`) do not match the pattern prefix; a non-V8 host yields no reason and stays `error`, as before. `validate-hook-body-compiles.ts`: the lowered-handler hint replaces the generic fix only (N3), and the `suppressWarnings` note is corrected (N1). The two gap pins and the hook split pin require a host refusal on Node 22 or older and tolerate a later V8 (N1 of the card). `quickjs-runner.ts`: as judged in ①; four pins plus the equality pin against a body that ran and threw (row #35715, #35720 N4). `action-body-wrapper.ts`, `checked-parse.ts`, `validate-hook-body-writes.ts` and its test: comment text only, true to the wrapper functions (N5).

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1 (nit) — one further missed refusal outside the stated residual: `/[\&\&]/v` compiles on V8 and QuickJS refuses it. It falls under the note's "syntax the host accepts and QuickJS does not"; no text is wrong.
- N2 (nit) — the `regexp-pattern` hint lists fixes for the card's six classes; a `v`-flag class error or a lone bracket under `u` gets the same list, none of which applies. The engine's sentence in the message still names the cause.
- N3 (nit) — `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/observe.ts` `BODY_THROW` reads only the `threw:` wrapper; no door relays the new hook or job sentence, so the grader's note is unaffected today. Outside the diff.

Rows: the card's ask is delivered except for S1's over-claim; row #35715 delivered (coded sentence, hook and job pinned); row #35720 N1 to N5 delivered.

## 维护者速读
- 这个 PR 让脚本里写错的正则在校验和发布时直接报错拦下;但契约审核发现极少数正则(几个较新的 Unicode 属性名)在运行时其实能跑,也会被误拦。
- 属于「钩子与动作脚本在发布时就拦下注定失败的写法」这条线。
- 需要开发再改一轮(只碰这一处判定和相关说明),改完再审;在此之前不合并。
- 无需你操作。

## 席位核对

Verdict: **REWORK** at head `81c369ca52a0fe89b5fd2edb4adeffd89f07a842` (read 2026-11-23T14:55Z).

1. **Shape.** Open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #35694`; fold rows #35715 and #35720 are named in the body and already closed as cards, so `Fixes` binds only the card. No closing keyword binds another card. Title carries `!`, body and changeset carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `mergeable_state: clean`.
2. **Premise measured.** `origin/main`: `judgeBodyCompile` sends every V8 pattern failure to `warning`, and the test pins `/(/` there; the runner coded a compile failure for actions only. Both premises held; the head moves both.
3. **Gates at this head (check-runs).** 62 success · 12 expected skip · 0 unexpected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success` (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36721`). `dogfood_battery` is pinned to this head, full (487 files, 4121 tests passed), no red.
4. **Why REWORK — the contract review's S1 is open on this head.** Record: PR comment 7104744143 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, tier verified on the reviewer's transcript, scope = every non-prose path). S1 (should-fix): V8's `Invalid property name` is a third reason on which the host refuses and QuickJS runs, and the rule sends it to `error`, so a body that runs is refused. Measured by the reviewer against quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0 with the same wrapper text: `\p{IDS_Unary_Operator}`, `\p{Modifier_Combining_Mark}`, `\p{sc=Katakana_Or_Hiragana}` (and their aliases) under `u`. Seat re-read of the V8 half on Node 22.23.5: all three answer `Invalid property name`, the same reason as `\p{Nope}`. A false refusal is the direction the card itself rules out ("the measured dialect gaps stay `warning`"), and the texts that promise it never happens are false as written: `18.body-regexp-pattern-refused.ts` (surface and reason), the module note of `validate-action-body-compiles.ts`, the `regexp-pattern` hint, `rule-explanations.ts`, and `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx` ("only the two pattern constructs … are a warning").
   **Asked:** keep `\p{Nope}/u` at `error` (a card pin) and stop refusing a property name QuickJS accepts. Preferred: a measured exception list of property names (V8 `Invalid property name`, QuickJS compiles) judged `warning` with the dialect gaps, pinned. Fallback only if that list cannot be measured honestly: keep `error` and make every text above say the property name is judged by the host's Unicode tables, naming the measured exceptions and the `new RegExp` way out in the hint. Either way the docs page and the ADR-0087 entry say what the code does. Then a delta contract review of the fix by the same reviewer (S1 closed by id) and my delta read.
5. **Also owed before landing (seat, not dev).** The claim 7097830473 is stale on two lines and must be amended on #35694 in the same round: `Clause-②: no` → `no (narrowing)` (the dev flagged the conflict and took the more specific arm, right), and the file surface gains the six text-only paths the PR body names (`validate-hook-body-writes.ts` and its test, `checked-parse.ts`, `hook-body.zod.ts`, `18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts`, `hook-bodies.mdx`). Each is a sentence this diff made false or that a fold row names, so none is an unclaimed adjacent fix. `Skills-docs: follow-up #36727` is honest (open, `Blocked-by: #36721`, names the exact sentence).
6. **Accepted as is (nits, no change asked).** L2 N1 (`/[\&\&]/v` is one more missed refusal, already covered by the note), N2 (the `regexp-pattern` hint's fix list fits the card's six classes only), N3 (`packages/qa/scenarios` `BODY_THROW` reads only `threw:`; outside the diff). Seat nit: `hook-bodies.mdx` says a non-compiling body from an artifact is reported as `hook 'NAME' does not compile` in a paragraph about hooks and jobs; a job reads `job 'NAME' …` — fold it into the S1 round if the paragraph is touched. Semver `minor` on lint, runtime and spec is accepted (runtime alone would stand at `patch`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6b0b9b3a8f8550296706888a7de5d8e14ad38828`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-regexp-literal-token-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.body-regexp-pattern-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.hook-job-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts, packages/lint/src/checked-parse.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-writes.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandboxed-action-crash-is-a-fault.test.ts

Delta review of the record on `81c369ca52a0fe89b5fd2edb4adeffd89f07a842` (PR comment 7104744143). Read: the diff from that head to this one (11 files: the changeset and one docs page, which are prose and not reviewed; five lint files; four semantic entries), the dev report 7122774685 as data, and the check-runs on this head. Every file outside the delta is byte-equal to the head the first record judged, so ①, ② and ③ of that record stand; only what the delta moves is judged again here.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: against the first head this delta only widens. A V8 `Invalid property name` (or `… in character class`) failure moves from `error` back to `warning` when every property escape the host refuses alone is one of twelve listed spellings, when no refused escape can be read out of the pattern, or when the host's Unicode tables are older than 17.0 or unnamed. Nothing moves from `warning` to `error`. Against `main` the PR is still a narrowing, now a smaller one. Right.
- Public surface: no export, shape member or schema key moves in the delta; `BodyCompileShape` is as the first record judged it. The four semantic entries change text only.
- Gates: 74 check-runs on this head, 62 `success`, 12 `skipped`, none failed or pending.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor` on lint, runtime and spec. The changeset body now states the property-name gap and the older-tables rule; `Skills-docs:` is untouched and #36727 still covers it (the skill sentence to write gains "or a property name only the runtime knows", a note for that card, not a finding here).

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev report carries no open question. Its one design choice, an older host warning on every refused property name, is answered in ④: accepted, it errs toward a missed refusal and the texts say so.
- SQL push-down: not applicable.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed

Why it holds, on the measured host (Node 22.23.5, Unicode 17.0):
- The eight spellings the first record measured, plus the four long-key forms of the script (`Script=`, `Script_Extensions=`), are the list; each now answers `regexp-dialect-gap` at `warning`, pinned bare under `u` and negated inside a class under `v`. The first round's sweep (every identifier in the QuickJS wasm, bare and under `sc=`, `scx=`, `gc=`, under `u`) found no other name, and it bounds the `v` and in-class forms too: V8 resolves a non-string property through the same lookup under either flag and in either position, and the string properties are accepted by both engines under `v` and refused by both under `u`.
- `/\p{Nope}/u` stays `error` (the card's done-when), and so does a listed name beside an unknown one, both pinned.
- An `error` on a property reason now requires an escape that the host refuses alone and that is off the list. Property-name validity does not depend on position, and the extraction regex admits only a `p` or `P` behind an odd run of backslashes, which under `u` or `v` is a property escape wherever a pattern may carry one; so such an escape is one QuickJS refuses too, by the sweep. No runnable body is refused on this path.

The read-back of the pattern from V8's sentence:
- Reason: the text after the last colon-space; V8's reasons carry none, so a pattern containing that text cannot shift it. The literal is what lies between the fixed prefix and the reason.
- Flags: after the last slash of the literal. Flags hold no slash, so a slash in the pattern (escaped, or bare inside a class) cannot shift the cut. `v` is chosen when the literal carries it, else `u`; no other flag set can produce a property reason.
- Escapes: an escaped backslash followed by `p{…}` is skipped (the lookbehind plus the paired-backslash run), `\P{…}` is read as its positive form, several escapes in one pattern are each judged, and nesting in a class changes nothing because the judgement is per name.
- Where the read finds no escape the host refuses alone (an unclosed `\p{`, a bare `\p`, a negated string property under `v`), the verdict is `warning`, never `error`.

The older-tables fallback reads `process.versions.unicode`; a missing, unparsable or lower value returns `warning` for every property reason. It can only miss a refusal. The CI pin asserts the pinned Node 22 carries 17.0, so the `\p{Nope}` pin is not silently weakened there.
